newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil evangelist sentenced for beating statue.
newsitem.headline: Brazil evangelist sentenced for beating statue.

text.p: A Brazilian evangelical preacher was sentenced to two years in prison for slapping and kicking a statue of the Virgin Mary during a nationally televised sermon, a newspaper reported on Thursday.
A Sao Paulo judge gave the sentence to Sergio von Helder, a member of the powerful and controversial Church of the Universal Kingdom of God, Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper said.
It added that Von Helder might not have to serve the full prison term because it was his first offence.
Court officials could not be reached to comment on the report because of the May Day labour holiday.
Von Helder was convicted of public disrespect for a religious symbol during the Oct. 12, 1995 televised sermon in which he lashed out at an effigy of Our Lady of Aparecida, Brazil's patron saint.
The incident outraged Roman Catholics in Brazil, the world's largest Catholic country, and provoked stone-throwing attacks on several Universal Church temples.

From humble beginnings in 1977 as an offshoot of the Pentecostal Church, the Universal Church has grown rich on donations from its mostly poor worshippers and is one of the main evangelical groups challenging the Catholic Church in Brazil.
It owns more than 2,000 churches in Brazil and around the world as well as television and radio stations, a newspaper and a bank. It also has representatives in Brazil's Congress.
